concept_name: Finding Directions by the Rising Sun

item.question: Lali faces the rising Sun on the school ground. She then turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. Which direction is she facing now, and which direction is behind her?
steps: Lali faces the rising Sun. The rising Sun is in the east, so she faces east.
Facing east, her left hand points north and her right hand points south.
She turns to face the direction her left hand was pointing to. That is north, so she now faces north.
Behind her is the opposite of north. North and south are opposite directions, so south is behind her.
Check: north is at the top of the compass rose and south is at the bottom, so they are opposite directions.
item.answer: She is facing north, and south is behind her

item.question: A playground picture has a compass with N at the top. A swing is at the top left, a slide at the top right, a sandpit at the bottom left and a seesaw at the bottom right. Which thing is east of the swing, south of the slide, west of the seesaw and north of the sandpit?
steps: The compass has N at the top, so above is north, below is south, the right is east and the left is west.
East of the swing: look to the right of the swing. The slide is there.
South of the slide: look below the slide. The seesaw is there.
West of the seesaw: look to the left of the seesaw. The sandpit is there.
North of the sandpit: look above the sandpit. The swing is there.
Check: the swing and the slide are in the top row and the sandpit and the seesaw are in the bottom row, and the top row is north of the bottom row.
item.answer: The slide is east of the swing, the seesaw is south of the slide, the sandpit is west of the seesaw and the swing is north of the sandpit

item.question: A girl stands at the centre of a room plan with a compass, N at the top. A table is above her, a bed is to the right of her, a door is below her and a cupboard is to the left of her. Say the direction of each thing from the girl. Then say in which direction the girl is from the bed.
steps: N is at the top, so above is north, the right is east, below is south and the left is west.
The table is above her, so the table is north of her.
The bed is to the right of her, so the bed is east of her.
The door is below her, so the door is south of her.
The cupboard is to the left of her, so the cupboard is west of her.
Now stand at the bed and look at the girl. She is to the left of the bed, so she is west of the bed.
Check: the bed is east of the girl and the girl is west of the bed, and east and west are opposite directions.
item.answer: The table is north, the bed east, the door south and the cupboard west of the girl. From the bed the girl is to the west

item.question: What is just south of the Basketball Court, across Market Road, and what is just north of it?
steps: A street map is a picture of roads and places seen from above. The compass has N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left.
Find the Basketball Court in the middle of the map. Market Road runs along the bottom of the court.
Go down the map, across Market Road. Down the map is south, so the place just south of the Basketball Court is the Shopping Centre.
Now go up the map from the court, across the small road above it. Up the map is north, so just north of the court is the block with the pond and Jaideep's House.
Turn it round. If the Shopping Centre is south of the court, then the court is north of the Shopping Centre.
Check with the compass: up is N, so north is up the map and south is down the map.
item.answer: The Shopping Centre is just south of the Basketball Court. The block with the pond and Jaideep's House is just north of it.

concept_name: Turning Right and Left on a Route

item.question: A cycle drives north along a road and turns left at a junction. Which direction is it driving after the turn? At the next junction it turns left again. Which direction is it driving now?
steps: The cycle drives north. Face north: your left hand points west and your right hand points east.
A left turn is a turn towards the left hand. The left hand points west, so after the first turn the cycle drives west.
Now the cycle drives west. Face west: your left hand points south.
The second left turn is towards south, so the cycle now drives south.
Check with the rule: a left turn takes north to west, and west to south.
The two left turns together made the cycle drive the opposite way to the way it started: it started north and now drives south.
item.answer: After the first left turn the cycle drives west. After the second left turn it drives south
item.text:
Worked example: A cycle drives north along a road and turns left at a junction. Which direction is it driving after the turn? At the next junction it turns left again. Which direction is it driving now?
